A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WeLore research despite substantial retitling and reorganization. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original gradient and weight analyses, compression perplexities, downstream fine-tuning results, and measured memory and throughput.

after.justification: V2 retains original WeLore experiments and adds Hessian-spectrum analyses, Mistral results, and application-task evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions use SVD, a global normalized-singular-value threshold targeting effective rank reduction, the same LRC classification rule, and LRC-only fine-tuning with N-LRCs frozen. WeLore-COMP and WeLore-PEFT name existing procedures; the new Hessian analysis does not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: V2 adds FreebaseQA factoid answering, CNN/DailyMail summarization across document lengths, and MT-Bench multi-turn conversation and instruction following (Table 2; Appendices D.4-D.5). These substantially broaden task coverage beyond the retained C4 and six reasoning benchmarks. The Wikitext-2 evaluation in v1 Appendix A.1 is removed.

E2.justification: SVD-LLM, cited but not evaluated in v1, becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Tables 2-3, including the retained C4 compression comparison. Existing uniform reduction, OWL, activation-SVD, fine-tuning, and pruning comparators remain in corresponding retained experiments. ActSVD/ASVD is a naming change, not another added baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces 25% rank-reduction application evaluations, GPT-4 judging against text-davinci-003 outputs, 300 summarization articles grouped by length, 80 MT-Bench questions, and Mistral-7B configurations. Pretraining diagnostics also change the illustrated layers and similarity measurement. For retained recovery results, v1 Table 1 states 7M training tokens while v2 Section 4.2 states 0.7M; v1 elsewhere already states 0.7M, so this is revised protocol reporting without evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: V2 adds Hessian-spectrum diagnostics investigating component and depth differences (Figure 1). It reworks pretraining analysis from raw-gradient cosine similarities and gradient spectra to gradient-subspace similarities paired with weight spectra, using different example layers (Figure 2). The LRC-versus-N-LRC ablation and pruning-combination analysis are retained; moving the latter to Appendix B is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates and does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result groups while retaining matched LLaMA benchmark scores. New Mistral results include perplexity 1351.32 before and 21.37 after fine-tuning at 50% rank reduction (Tables 1 and 4). Table 2 newly reports WeLore versus SVD-LLM scores of 71.89 versus 71.95 for factoid QA and 6.09 versus 5.79 for conversation. V1's Wikitext-2 results and detailed fine-tuning GPU-memory rows are removed.

T1.justification: V2 adds Hessian-eigenspace stabilization and gradient-alignment theorems, proof sketches, and extensive Appendix A derivations. Their assumptions include Hessian Lipschitz continuity, a Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz condition, a spectral gap, and reversible structure. V1 contains no corresponding formal convergence or alignment results.

C1.justification: V2 makes a theoretical explanation through Hessian analysis a central contribution in its abstract, introduction, and conclusion. V1 principally presents empirical gradient observations and a conjectured connection to low-rank weights. The claims about nonuniform compression and efficient LRC-only fine-tuning remain.

C2.justification: V1 explains compressibility through continuing gradient variation versus early gradient saturation. V2 develops a substantially different explanation involving Hessian gaps and gradient-subspace stabilization, including softmax, gating, and layer-depth mechanisms. It also acknowledges the new factoid-QA shortfall against SVD-LLM. V1's explicit limitation concerning unexplored WeLore training from scratch disappears.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1 Tables 7-9: precomputed thresholds, checkpoint download links, and detailed continual/downstream training configurations, including learning rates, batch sizes, precision, schedules, and sample counts. It adds article-selection and judging details for the new application evaluations. The threshold-selection algorithm and code-access statement remain, but reproducibility documentation changes substantially.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around explanations of low-rank emergence, discussing low-dimensional data and implicit rank regularization through works by Timor, Ergen and Pilanci, Ongie and Willett, Ji and Telgarsky, Le and Jegelka, and Galanti. V1's framing centers more directly on GaLore and compression methods. Much existing compression and fine-tuning related work is retained in Appendix C.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its introduction substantially rewritten, and its narrative reorganized around theory, observations, and applications. Compression and fine-tuning become subsections with separate names; experiments are restructured around explicit questions. Related work and implementation material move to appendices, alongside author and publication-header changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and extensively restructures displays. It adds Hessian plots and application tables, replaces the pretraining diagnostic panels, and redraws the seven-component singular-value figure as four panels. V1 Table 1 is split across compression and recovery tables, several displays move to appendices, and the threshold and hyperparameter tables disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens empirical support through new tasks, Mistral, and SVD-LLM comparisons, but removes important reproducibility tables and detailed fine-tuning memory evidence. Its new central alignment guarantee also has a substantive proof gap: Appendix A.3 does not justify absorbing the additive K eta^2 term between Eqs. (28)-(29), and bounded gradient norms alone do not establish relative alignment when the denominator can vanish. These empirical gains and losses in reproducibility and theoretical reliability prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
